title: Instance-Aware Test-Time Segmentation for Continual Domain Shifts (CoTICA)
mechanism: Pseudo-label thresholds adapt per class and per image from that image's own confidence distribution, and learning is re-weighted toward the classes most hurt by the shift.
adaptation: Use per-cell crack and inactive thresholds from the cell's confidence quantiles instead of a global 0.95, as the pseudo-label rule inside the SGP-TTA or A3-TTA arms. This targets the 'confident background on faint cracks' failure seen in our SSL nulls.
min_experiment: Arm: row 3 or 8 with quantile thresholds. Baseline: the same arm with a fixed threshold. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.01 over the parent arm.
evidence: R: outperforms prior CTTA and TTA methods in eight segmentation scenarios, including synthetic-to-real and long-term shifts (numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: None at test time. Class-aware thresholds were proposed in an earlier SSL null diagnosis but never run.
